reviews.body:
Two related places have the same one-way rule:
- `convert-posix` (`cmd/internal/gwcli/utils.go:399`) has its own `filepath.Rel` check that also accepts a sidecar containing the root. Please reuse the same helper so both commands agree.
- `extra/example.conf` says nothing about nesting for `VGW_META_SIDECAR`, and `VGW_VERSIONING_DIR` only says "must NOT be a subdirectory". Please document "must not be the same as, inside, or contain the root directory".

review_comments.body: While fixing this: the comparison uses `filepath.Abs` only, so a symlinked path segment hides nesting in both directions. Root `/d/link/gwroot` (`link -> real`) with sidecar `/d/real/gwroot/inner` is accepted, and so is the reverse. Both dirs must exist anyway, so please compare `filepath.EvalSymlinks` of both. That also handles macOS `/tmp` vs `/private/tmp`.

Nit: with this message gone, a bad `--sidecar` now fails with "the root directory X contains the directory Y", which doesn't say which flag is wrong (`validateSubDir` is shared with `--versioning-dir`). Please wrap it at the call sites, e.g. `fmt.Errorf("invalid sidecar directory: %w", err)` and the same for the versioning dir.

This passes on any error, e.g. a stat failure if `inside` weren't created. Please assert the nesting error itself (a sentinel checked with `errors.Is`, or at least the message).

Please also make it table-driven and add cases for:
- sidecar == root (rejected)
- sidecar is the parent / an ancestor of root (rejected, after the fix above)
- symlinked path hiding the nesting (rejected)
- root `.` with sidecar `../s3-sidecar` in default (non-AbsolutePaths) mode (accepted; main rejected this too), using `t.Chdir`
- trailing separator on the root
This uses `meta.XattrMeta{}` with `SideCarDir` set, a combination the CLI never builds. Please use `meta.NewSideCar(sibling)` so the test runs the real sidecar setup.

This now also changes `--versioning-dir` validation (a parent of the root or the root itself is newly rejected, and scoutfs goes through the same path), but there is no versioning test. Please add `VersioningDir` cases: parent of root / equal / inside → `ErrDirsNested`, sibling → accepted. Please also assert the `invalid sidecar directory:` / `invalid versioning directory:` prefix, since naming the flag was the point of that change.

The walk up to the closest existing ancestor isn't needed. Every caller requires both dirs to exist: `validateSubDir` stats `dir` right after this check, the root is chdir'ed into or opened, and convert-posix stats the root and calls `NewSideCar` right after. Moving the `os.Stat` in `validateSubDir` before the nesting check and calling `filepath.EvalSymlinks` on both paths directly would drop this function and `TestCheckDirsNotNestedMissingDir`. It also removes the `real` variable that shadows the builtin (line 629).

Nit: the message currently reads "invalid sidecar directory: /d and the root directory /d/gwroot: directory must not be the same as, inside, or contain the root directory".`ErrDirsNested = errors.New("must not be the same as, inside, or contain the root directory")` and `fmt.Errorf("%v %w %v", dir, ErrDirsNested, root)`, which gives "invalid sidecar directory: /d must not be the same as, inside, or contain the root directory /d/gwroot".

Nit: if symlinks can't be created (e.g. Windows without the privilege), this skips the whole table, including the non-symlink cases. Please create the symlink only in the symlink cases, or move them to their own test. Also `real` on line 51 shadows the builtin; `realDir` would be clearer.

Nit: with `AbsolutePaths` (no chdir), a missing root now fails here first and gets blamed on the other flag: `invalid versioning directory: resolve "/x/typo": lstat /x/typo: no such file or directory`. Without the flag it's `open /x/typo: ...`. Saying `resolve root directory %q` here would make that clear. Also, the doc comment on line 594 has a doubled "so": "...cannot hide the nesting, so both must exist".

comments.body: This won't automatically run in continuous integration without approval. A member of the Versity organization must allow it.

Thanks for the thorough review, all points are addressed in the new commit:
- `validateSubDir` now rejects equal, inside, and containing directories (two-way check), so it also covers `--versioning-dir`; the repro (`--sidecar /d /d/gwroot`) is now refused at startup.
- Both paths are compared after `EvalSymlinks`, resolving through the closest existing ancestor when a path does not exist yet.
- The nesting error is the sentinel `posix.ErrDirsNested` and is wrapped at the call sites as `invalid sidecar directory: ...` / `invalid versioning directory: ...`.
- `convert-posix` now calls the same exported helper (`posix.CheckDirsNotNested`) so both commands agree.
- `extra/example.conf` documents "must not be the same as, inside, or contain" for `VGW_META_SIDECAR` and `VGW_VERSIONING_DIR`.
- `sidecardir_test.go` is table-driven with `errors.Is` assertions and covers sidecar == root, ancestor of root, symlinked nesting in both directions, trailing separator, and root `.` with `../s3-sidecar` via `t.Chdir`; it uses `meta.NewSideCar`.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Addressed the latest review in the new commit:
- Dropped the closest-existing-ancestor walk (and its test): `validateSubDir` now stats the directory before the nesting check, and `CheckDirsNotNested` calls `filepath.EvalSymlinks` on both paths.
- The error now reads `invalid sidecar directory: <dir> must not be the same as, inside, or contain the root directory <root>`.
- The nesting tests run each case for both `--sidecar` and `--versioning-dir`, asserting `ErrDirsNested` and the flag prefix.
- Symlink cases are in their own test, so a platform without symlink support only skips those; `real` is renamed to `realDir`.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Addressed both nits in the new commit: a root that cannot be resolved now reports `resolve root directory "...": ...`, and the doubled "so" in the `CheckDirsNotNested` doc comment is reworded.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Good catch. The new commit compares by file identity (`os.SameFile` walking up the parents, as in your snippet), which replaces the string-prefix check, so `isDirBelowRoot` is removed. `TestAuxDirNestingCaseInsensitive` covers inside / same / parent with a different case and skips on case-sensitive filesystems; run on a case-insensitive NTFS mount, its cases fail without the fix and pass with it. Bind mounts were not tested separately.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
